study_identification_part.si4_title: Lifespan development of thalamic nuclei and characterizing thalamic nuclei abnormalities in schizophrenia using normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Model lifespan developmental trajectories of thalamic nuclei volumes using normative modeling and quantify individual-level deviations in an independent schizophrenia cohort; assess associations with cognition.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: HCP S1200; HCP Development Lifespan; HCP Aging Lifespan
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states that normative modeling was conducted using data from three independent HCP Lifespan Studies: the original HCP S1200 sample (ages 21-35), HCP Development Lifespan 2.0 release (ages 5-21), and HCP Aging Lifespan 2.0 release (ages 36-100+). These three datasets were combined to create normative models across the lifespan.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Normative modeling of thalamic nuclei development was conducted using data from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) Lifespan Studies (combined n = 2490). The HCP Lifespan studies include three independent large-scale, publicly available population-based samples of typically developing individuals covering the human lifespan from ages 5-100+: the original HCP S1200 sample (ages 21-35, n = 1113); HCP Development Lifespan (2.0 release, ages 5-21, n = 652); and HCP Aging Lifespan (2.0 release, ages 36-100+, n = 725).
rci1_dataset_name.location: Huang2024.pdf.md: Methods / Study participants and procedures / Human Connectome Project Lifespan cohort, L68-L69

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper states that after randomly removing twins and excluding individuals with poor quality scans or segmentation failures, the final sample was 1952 (HCP S1200 n=825, Development HCP n=525, Aging HCP n=725). This is the number used for normative modeling.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: After randomly removing twins to avoid biasing the normative lifespan model and excluding individuals with poor quality scans or segmentation failures, the final sample was 1952 (HCP S1200 n = 825, Development HCP n = 525, Aging HCP n = 725).
rci2_hc_n.location: Huang2024.pdf.md: Methods / Study participants and procedures / Human Connectome Project Lifespan cohort, L70

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Up to ~18% of individuals with schizophrenia showed infra-normal (below 5th centile) mediodorsal and pulvinar volumes; deviations (centiles), but not raw volumes, correlated with cognitive impairment severity.
